name: Trumaí
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_quote: Stress always falls on the final syllable of the word. Phonetic correlates of stress are greater intensity and higher pitch than preceding syllables. (Guirardello 1999)

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Coding fixed-strict final stress rests on the standard reference grammar (Guirardello 1999, Rice PhD, 452 pp), which we hold as the original Rice bitstream plus scanned; the deciding sentence 'Stress always falls on the final syllable of the word' is verified verbatim at printed p.7 (p.33), and the grammar's other stress remarks (postpositions independently stressed, p.75; stressed vs cliticized auxiliary allomorphs, p.141) do not disturb a word-domain final-stress coding. No phonetic/prosodic study of Trumai exists in Crossref or SAPhon, and the only newer description is a 2023 handbook sketch by the same author (paywalled). The record's top-level quote/cite/grade fields are empty while the verified primary quotation sits in sources[0]; promote it to the deciding quote and set the strength of the evidence to primary-verified. If the blank grade is by design for database-derived rows, action is 'n

tone.quote: O acento em Trumai é fixo. ocorrendo sempre na sílaba final de uma palavra. Os correlatos fonéticos de acento nessa língua são uma maior intensidade e um tom mais alto que o das sílabas anteriores: (2) a. [t̪si.ˈpup] 'lenha' b. [pi.ˈkɛ] 'casa' c. [wa.ru.ˈt̪a] 'abóbora' (scanned text layer; 'fixo.' = 'fixo,' in print; example transcriptions normalised from the scanned)
tone.locator: p. 209, section FONOLOGIA, B. Acento; phonology section pp. 198-213; postposition stress p. 251 (L. Posposições)
tone.translation: Stress in Trumai is fixed, always falling on the final syllable of a word. The phonetic correlates of stress in this language are greater intensity and a higher pitch than that of the preceding syllables: (2) a. 'firewood' b. 'house' c. 'pumpkin'.
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.summary: No tones: the description posits no tonal contrasts; word prosody is fixed word-final stress realised as greater intensity plus raised pitch; postpositions are free forms with their own stress. Tone-bearing units, downstep, melodies: not applicable / not discussed.
